translationRepairs: Neqin; Fu Heng; [their sons] Fu Ling'an and Fu Long'an; Fu Long'an's son Feng Shenjilun; Fu Chang'an
Neqin; Fu Heng; Fu Heng's sons Fu Ling'an and Fu Long'an; Fu Long'an's son Feng Shenjilun; Fu Chang'an
Heading 傅恆子福靈安福隆安 attaches 子 to 傅恆 alone, so Fu Ling'an and Fu Long'an are Fu Heng's sons; '[their sons]' wrongly shared them with Neqin. The proposed idiomatic restores that kinship.
Neqin, of the Niohuru clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner and a great-grandson of Ebilun.
Neqin, of the Niohuru clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner and a great-grandson of Eidu.
s0003 has 額亦都曾孫; 額亦都 is Eidu. Ebilun is 遏必隆, named only in s0004 as Yinde's father. The proposed idiomatic corrects the great-grandfather.
Neqin, of the Niohuru clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, a great-grandson of Ebilun.
Neqin, of the Niohuru clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, a great-grandson of Eidu.
The same Chinese 額亦都曾孫 was misrendered as Ebilun in the literal field; Eidu is the correct English for 額亦都.
That December an edict praised Neqin's diligence; in recognition of the empress dowager's kin, he was raised to duke of the first rank.
That December an edict praised Neqin's diligence; in recognition of Empress Xiaozhaoren's maternal kin, he was raised to duke of the first rank.
Chinese 推孝昭仁皇后外家恩 names Empress Xiaozhaoren's maternal clan; 'empress dowager's kin' invents a living dowager and drops the named empress.
When Zhili governor Li Wei accused river director Zhu Zao of fraud and corruption, Neqin and Minister Sun Jia'en were sent to investigate; Zhu was sentenced to exile.
When Zhili governor Li Wei accused river director Zhu Zao of fraud and corruption, Neqin and Minister Sun Jiagan were sent to investigate; Zhu was sentenced to exile.
孫嘉淦 is Sun Jiagan (淦 = gàn); Jia'en misreads the final character. The proposed idiomatic restores the correct name.

Zhili Governor Li Wei impeached Director-General of Rivers Zhu Zao for fraud, oppression, and corruption; Neqin was ordered with Minister Sun Jia'en to investigate and try the case; Zhu was sentenced to banishment.

Zhili Governor Li Wei impeached Director-General of Rivers Zhu Zao for fraud, oppression, and corruption; Neqin was ordered with Minister Sun Jiagan to investigate and try the case; Zhu was sentenced to banishment.
Literal likewise had Sun Jia'en for 孫嘉淦; Jiagan is the correct reading of 嘉淦.
Neqin and Jia'en also submitted a detailed memorial on sluices and dams along both banks of the Yongding River.
Neqin and Jiagan also submitted a detailed memorial on sluices and dams along both banks of the Yongding River.
Short form 嘉淦 in s0019 is the same Sun Jiagan; Jia'en repeats the misreading of 淦.
Neqin, together with Jia'en, memorialized item by item on building sluices and dams along the north and south banks of the Yongding River.
Neqin, together with Jiagan, memorialized item by item on building sluices and dams along the north and south banks of the Yongding River.
Literal short name Jia'en for 嘉淦 is the same error; Jiagan matches 孫嘉淦.

In the fourth month of 1747 he was sent to Shanxi to join Governor Ai Bida in trying Zhang Shilu of Wanmin, Zhang Yuan of Anyi, and others who had led mobs against officials; all were sentenced by law.

In the fourth month of 1747 he was sent to Shanxi to join Governor Ai Bida in trying Zhang Shilu of Wanquan, Zhang Yuan of Anyi, and others who had led mobs against officials; all were sentenced by law.
萬全民 is a man of Wanquan; Wanmin misreads 全. The proposed idiomatic restores the county name.

In the fourth month of the twelfth year he was ordered to Shanxi to join Governor Ai Bida in trying the case of Zhang Shilu of Wanmin and Zhang Yuan of Anyi and others who led crowds in resisting officials; judgment was according to law.

In the fourth month of the twelfth year he was ordered to Shanxi to join Governor Ai Bida in trying the case of Zhang Shilu of Wanquan and Zhang Yuan of Anyi and others who led crowds in resisting officials; judgment was according to law.
Literal likewise rendered 萬全 as Wanmin; Wanquan is the correct place-name reading.
He also said supervising the army at attack on Ali Mountain—having returned to camp, our several score men scattered each like birds and beasts.
He also said that while supervising the assault on Ali Mountain, after he had returned to camp, several dozen of our men scattered each like birds and beasts.
Chinese 既回營，我軍數十人各鳥獸散 means after he had returned to camp, several dozen men scattered. The old literal is ungrammatical and obscures that sequence; the proposal fixes both.
His father Li Rongbao is treated in the biography of his father Misanhan.
His father Li Rongbao is treated in the biography of Misanhan, Li Rongbao's father.
其父米思翰 refers to Li Rongbao's father Misanhan, not Fu Heng's father. The chained second 'his father' wrongly makes Misanhan Fu Heng's father; the proposal clarifies the chain.
In March 1748 Empress Xiaoxianchun died at Dezhou on the southern tour; Fu Heng had accompanied the emperor and directed the mourning rites.
In March 1748 Empress Xiaoxianchun accompanied the emperor on a southern tour and died at Dezhou on the return; Fu Heng had accompanied the journey and directed the mourning rites.
Chinese 從上南巡，還至德州崩 states she accompanied the southern tour and died on the return at Dezhou. The old idiomatic omits both accompaniment and return; the proposal restores them.
Fu Heng and Yue Zhongqi chose to push deep; Slob Dpon sent headmen to sue for peace, and Fu Heng ordered him bound to camp.
Fu Heng and Yue Zhongqi chose to push deep; Slob Dpon sent headmen to sue for peace, and Fu Heng ordered him to bind himself and come to camp.
令自縛詣軍門 is an order that Slob Dpon bind himself and come to headquarters, not that others bind him and bring him. The proposal restores the reflexive 自縛.

Fu Heng declined the four-dragon patch but was ordered to wear it; a ancestral hall was built after the precedents of Ebilun and Tong Guowei, Li Rongbao was given a posthumous title, and a mansion was granted inside the East Gate.

Fu Heng declined the four-dragon patch but was ordered to wear it; an ancestral hall was built after the precedents of Eidu and Tong Guowei, Li Rongbao was given a posthumous title, and a mansion was granted inside the East Gate.
用額亦都、佟國維故事 cites Eidu (額亦都), not Ebilun. The proposal corrects the name and the article before ancestral hall.

Fu Heng memorialized to decline the four-dragon patch; the emperor ordered him to wear it at audience and again, following the precedents of Ebilun and Tong Guowei, ordered a ancestral hall built to sacrifice from his great-grandfather Hashitun downward, posthumously enfeoffed Li Rongbao with a title, granted a residence inside the East Gate, and composed a poem on its completion.

Fu Heng memorialized to decline the four-dragon patch; the emperor ordered him to wear it at audience and again, following the precedents of Eidu and Tong Guowei, ordered an ancestral hall built to sacrifice from his great-grandfather Hashitun downward, posthumously granted Li Rongbao a posthumous name, granted a residence inside the East Gate, and composed a poem on its completion.
Literal had the same Ebilun error for 額亦都, and 追予李榮保諡 is granting a posthumous name (諡), not an enfeoffment. The proposal corrects both.
In the seventh month he died; the emperor poured libation at his house, gave him a prince's funeral, and posthumous title Wenzong.
In the seventh month he died; the emperor poured libation at his house, gave him a prince's funeral, and posthumous title Wenzhong.
諡文忠 is the posthumous name Wenzhong; Wenzong would be 文宗. The proposed idiomatic restores 忠.

In the seventh month he died; the emperor personally visited his house to pour libation, ordered funeral rites equal to a clansman prince of the blood of the third degree, and gave the posthumous title Wenzong.

In the seventh month he died; the emperor personally visited his house to pour libation, ordered funeral rites equal to a clansman prince of the blood of the third degree, and gave the posthumous title Wenzhong.
Literal likewise misread 文忠 as Wenzong; Wenzhong is correct.
In 1796 Fukang'an's pacification of the Miao won Fu Heng a posthumous beile rank.
In 1796 Fukang'an's pacification of the Miao won Fu Heng a posthumous beizi rank.
贈貝子 is posthumous beizi rank; beile is 貝勒. The proposed idiomatic corrects the noble rank.
In the first year of Jiaqing, because Fukang'an pacified the Miao, Fu Heng was posthumously given the rank of beile.
In the first year of Jiaqing, because Fukang'an pacified the Miao, Fu Heng was posthumously given the rank of beizi.
Literal likewise had beile for 貝子; beizi is the correct rank term.
Fulong'an married Princess Hejia and became prince consort and personal guard.
Fulong'an married the Gaozong Emperor's daughter Princess Hejia and was appointed prince consort of the first rank and imperial bodyguard.
御前侍衛 is an imperial bodyguard; “guard of the person” is opaque and can imply the wrong person was guarded.
Fuchang'an rose from blue-feathered guard to vice banner general of the Bordered Red Banner, armory director, and household head.
Fuchang'an rose from blue-feathered guard to vice banner general of the Plain Red Banner Manchus, armory director, and head of the Imperial Household.
正紅旗滿洲副都統 is vice banner general of the Plain Red Banner Manchus; Bordered would be 鑲紅旗, and 滿洲 was dropped. 領內務府 is head of the Imperial Household. The proposal restores these.
Fuchang'an rose from guard with the blue feather to vice banner general of the Bordered Red Banner Manchus, director of the Armory, and head of the Imperial Household.
Fuchang'an rose from guard with the blue feather to vice banner general of the Plain Red Banner Manchus, director of the Armory, and head of the Imperial Household.
Literal likewise had Bordered Red for 正紅旗; Plain Red Banner Manchus matches the Chinese.
In 1816 he became vice banner general of the Bordered Yellow Banner Manchus.
In 1816 he became vice banner general of the Plain Yellow Banner Manchus.
正黃旗滿洲副都統 is the Plain Yellow Banner; Bordered Yellow is 鑲黃旗. The proposed idiomatic corrects the banner.
In the twenty-first year he was appointed vice banner general of the Bordered Yellow Banner Manchus.
In the twenty-first year he was appointed vice banner general of the Plain Yellow Banner Manchus.
Literal likewise misread 正黃旗 as Bordered Yellow; Plain Yellow is correct.
